title: Nuclear bomb in space would disable 98 per cent of satellites within a week | New Scientist
description: Just one nuclear explosion in space would have global and long-lasting repercussions, disabling almost every satellite and creating technological chaos from which it would take years to recover, warn experts
author: Matthew Sparkes

title: Massive data centres collectively use as much electricity as an entire US state | New Scientist
description: The largest data centres in the US are responsible for about 2 per cent of the country's entire annual electricity use
author: Madeleine Cuff

title: Skeleton found in Denmark came from man who witnessed the arrival of farming | New Scientist
description: Clues about the diet of “Rødhals Man”, who lived some 6000 years ago, hint that he lived through one of the most revolutionary changes in human history
author: Chris Simms

title: Noise pollution is reshaping the health and behaviour of animals everywhere | New Scientist
description: There is almost nowhere on Earth free from disruptive human noise – but it's one of the easiest environmental problems to solve
author: Madeleine Cuff

title: Did El Niño cause an early breakdown in the polar vortex? | New Scientist
description: The polar vortex winds have undergone an unprecedented weakening, which could bring cold weather to Europe. Some scientists suspect the record El Niño is to blame
author: Alec Luhn

title: Researchers build the first ever quantum clock that uses sunlight | New Scientist
description: Quantum clocks usually rely on advanced lasers and isolated atoms in the lab, but a new experiment showed that the same clock design can work with sunlight instead
author: Karmela Padavic-Callaghan
